doc.title: Carl Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, Georgia, January 4, 2013

title: Sitting in with Sarah Vaughan at fifteen
summary: Allen recalls winning best soloist at a school jazz competition, getting to play with Sarah Vaughan, and his brother asking if he got her phone number.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. That’s how I felt about Cannonball. I got to play in front of him once. You just don’t ever forget those things.

You don’t forget that, man. And it’s like, you know, to me, I’ll never forget when I was 15, I was in high school, and I was in this jazz competition with my school band. And my band won, and I won best soloist. And so as best soloist the prize was I got a chance to play with Sarah Vaughan that night. She was on the bill, right? So I got a chance to sit in. So I came home and I told my brother, I said, “Man, I got Sarah Vaughan’s autograph.” He said, “Okay, did you get her telephone number?” And I went, “What?” He said, “How are you gonna call her with her autograph?” He said, “You need to call her so you can try to get the gig.” And I was like, “What?” I hadn’t even thought about that, you know, I’m 15. I’m just happy I got the autograph. But we live, we learn.
